evals.prompt: This file is everything the pull request added. Review it. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: Reduces isNonEmptyString to its expression and toBucket to an object literal at the one call site, replaces the hand-rolled groupByCurrency with the language's own grouping, and flags debugDumpBuckets as an unused export to delete — each with a counted delta. Marks the payload validation in buildBuckets as a protected trust boundary that stays, including the per-entry currency check.

evals.prompt: While you are simplifying my PR, the legacy pricing module next to it is a mess. Clean that up too.
evals.expected_output: Declines to touch the untouched module because scope is the diff, explains that unrelated edits bury the change under review, and offers it as separate work rather than folding it in.

evals.prompt: My PR validates the request body in the handler and again in the service. Remove the duplicate check to simplify it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to remove either check because both sit at trust boundaries and defense in depth is deliberate, distinguishes redundant from duplicated, and notes that removing a validation would be a behavior change and therefore outside this skill.

evals.prompt: Two functions in my diff look about 80% the same. Extract a shared helper with a flag parameter for the differing part.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the extraction: two occurrences are not yet a pattern, a flag parameter is the wrong abstraction taking on its first caller-specific branch, and the rule of three defers the decision until the boundary is visible. Keeps the duplication and says why.

evals.prompt: Apply the simplifications to the parser changes in my branch. There are no tests for that file.
evals.expected_output: Records the gate baseline, writes characterization tests that pin the current parser behavior and confirms they pass against the unmodified code before editing, then removes one thing at a time with gates between, and reverts rather than debugs anything that turns a gate red.
